Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Okay, this paper towel represents the space-time continuum. Normally, it moves in a straight line, (he puts the paper towel on a hook) but something has disrupted the flow. Now time cannot move forward and it puts enormous strain on the fabric of time (tears the paper towel) and tears the fabric! So now there is a little less space-time fabric to work with. The days are getting shorter. Now, you take this shortened piece of space-time (puts the paper towel on the hook and tears it again) and loop it again. Do this enough times (crumples the paper towel and puts it in his pocket) and pretty soon you do not have anything left. What I cannot seem to figure out is what could have possibly caused the space-time disruption in the first place? And an even bigger conundrum is how Candace is standing outside of the space-time interruption and somehow knew about its effects.

Name: Baljeet-2
Dialog: That's Dr. Baljeet to you. Were you not listening? Here is the crux of your problem. Think of the universe and all of the many dimensions as circular. The energy flows between the dimensions like this, clockwise. Say this is your dimension, and this is our dimension. You traveled with the flow of energy, so going clockwise would be easy. Going counterclockwise would take 8 million gigawatts of energy, overloading the local power grid. I have prepared a little song to help illustrate my point. (he plays an accordion)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Right? Then I started thinking about how important it is to make the right decision on everything! You see, every choice carries with it its own potential timeline. So every decision I make effectively nullifies the possible future! I can not even choose which flavour of ice-cream to order. If I choose vanilla, that may set me on the path to the presidency. But if I have strawberry, I could get hit by a bus!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Okay, everyone. Please return your seats to the upright position, and please do not panic. As you can see the Paper Pelican is dissolving in water, because it is, after all, made of paper mache. But do not worry, because your seat cushions also function as flotation devices. Thank you for flying with us.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Stabby Barf Pain is the name of a theoretical fifth season that combines the best aspects of the other four seasons, winter, spring, summer, and fall into one! Flowers bloom as golden leaves fall from trees. Warm sun shines as beautiful snowflakes fill the air. A fifth season beyond all expectations!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I signed up for a class called "Summer Rocks," believing it was a geology course. It turned out to be a rock-and-roll camp, and no matter how hard I study, I just do not rock! I could actually get an e- (tries to say "F") an- Oh, I can't even say that terrible letter. Ineas! Erb! What am I going to do?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (growls) That is it! I can put up with noogies, wedgies, wet willies, and even the fact that you apparently placed a tracking device on, or inside, my person, but I will not tolerate your ignorant decision to take plastic over paper! From this moment on, I am no longer your nerd!! (storms out)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: NOOOOO! If time stops looping, there will be no big tears in the fabric of space-time and no way for us to get home. We must find a way to get ourselves and that machine through one of the rifts and back into Danville. Then we can push the button and blow up the machine.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I have! You see, the greatest impediment to making astronomical observations, is our atmosphere. It is like looking through pea soup! So to make our terrestrial telescopes more effective, I am going to take all of the Earth's atmosphere, and put it on the moon! (shows poster that shows what he's saying)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Hello, everyone. I was just cleaning my room and I thought I would return some of the things Ferb lent me. Your cowboy hat, your baseball mitt, your banjo CDs, your American flag unitard, oh, and here's your bald eagle. (Gives all the things in order and when Baljeet says bald eagle, it flies away) Oh, and Phineas, here is your sack.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (Narrating) In 1903, my great-grandfather was leading a bicycle race, when he fell into a tiger pit. Years later, my grandfather skillfully avoided the tiger pit, but sadly not the tiger. Then, my father was confident he had outsmarted the tiger, but he was wrong.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I was just giving Buford some pointers on collegiate life. Since I've already graduated and been accepted as a professor, I could pull some strings and get him into my school. (to Buford) Just think, Buford. You could be my student! I would be the boss of you!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Excellent! And I have repurposed my portable particle accelerator science project (which took second place? Hello?!) to track Mrs. Flynn-Fletcher's essence. Even under optimal conditions, I calculated she can only hang together for another eight minutes and forty-seven seconds!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I did. (Clears his throat) We Speckies vow to live in peace and harmony with you Finkies. All we ask is that you admit Space Adventure is much better than Stumbleberry Finkbat, and that you have brought eternal shame to your families forever believing otherwise.

Name: Baljeetolas
Dialog: Listen, here is how it works. By observing the swamp, logic tells me that it is too big to go around. And by gathering information about it from Isabel, I can logically make assessments about the best way to get across. Are you following me?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Well, that was very entertaining, but that is all I had time scheduled for. (notices how high they are) Oh, wait. You are already airborne. And I am already still with you. (begins to panic a little) I can not believe this! My schedule is totally blown! I am going to miss my polka recital!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Well, first, I would like you to iron all of my books, then perhaps polish my retainer, then you can start my college applications. Massage my toosties. Sew my name onto my underwear, organize my book reports by subject. Ooh, build me—

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: The diameter of the sun can be calculated from the distance between the Earth and the sun. Since we know the time taken by the Earth to go once around the sun, p=1 year, and the distance traveled by the Earth in this process, 2πa...

Name: Baljeet-2
Dialog: (pauses) I know, it needs a chorus. Anyway, without the 8 million gigawatts, you would have to go clockwise, the long way around. Theoretically, you would get home, but there is no telling how many dimensions you would have to go through.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Actually, I can think of many things that I can not do. Flying comes to mind. Also putting my foot behind my head, but it occurs to me that you're speaking hyperbolically. So point taken, Greg LeMond! I'm going to win this race!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (outraged) I do not believe this! I wasted all this time in a class without grades?!? Aohhhhh! If only there were some other kind of outlet for me to express these feelings to my like-minded peer group! (comes to a realization. peeks at the stage than to Coltrane.) Pardon me! I want to try something! (Runs and stomps onto stage. Their song "Gimme a Grade" plays. As they continue with the song, the audience sway and move their heads along with the beat.)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Huh? Oh, sorry. I am too preoccupied with today's wild fluctuations in the space-time continuum. With pressure readings like this, I could potentially get sucked into a rift. And then none of you would remember I ever existed!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (over radio) Phineas! Good news, I have the device that turned your mom into the cloud and I am trying to reverse it! But the battery is not working so we are having to run an extension cord from your house. Can you get the Mom Cloud here?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Now Buford, your mindless bullying may have a rustic charm stateside, but now we are in Europe. A place of high refinement. So let me do all the talking. (They go inside a restaurant and speaks with a man in a different accent) Excuse me, sir. Would you have any used cooking oil that we could have?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Because today is the Tri-State Area Unification Day! I learned all about it in Assimilation class. You see, the Tri-State Area was the bi-state area until our founder, the great John P. Trystate, uttered the immortal words:

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: W-what? Uh, uh, oh. Thank you. (Flashlight switch flips; Wolf howls) Well, this is a story about a kid who comes to this country, and goes to camp. He, like, has to share a tent with a bully. It's really quite terrifying, actually. Quite terrifying. (Crickets chirp; Flashlight switch flips)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Technology like that is twenty years away; you will need a time machine. Luckily, I have been working on a design. I have not figured out all the quantum physics yet, but if you give me a couple of days...

Name: Baljeet Replicas
Dialog: (All at once) He is always giving us a hard time...He says he is our friend! Would a friend steal your bike?! To be fair, he stole everyone's bike...And what about the time he drank all the water out of our fish tank?!

Name: Baljeetolas
Dialog: I have an idea. I think I have a way to get you across this swamp. I have been working on a way of solving problems by the process of deriving reliable generalizations from observation. I call it "logic."

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Based on his extensive history of malapropisms, I would say that he is talking about the Chupacabra, the Latin American goat sucker, that is said to haunt the deserts of Mexico and South-Western America.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Useless Shoelace Facts, Volume 8. "The plastic or metal tip on the end of a shoelace is called an... aglet. A-G-L-E-T. It is one of the most useful, yet tragically ignored inventions in all of history".

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Well, they must have disappeared through a temporal rift. If we could calculate the location of the next rift, we could just throw in a rope with a life preserver tied to the end of it and pull it out.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Yes. They do a tail-wagging dance to alert each other to a source of food. (in background) The waggle explains the angle to the destination in relations to the imaginary line between the sun and the door of the hive.

Name: Nerdcrow (Baljeet)
Dialog: I am a nerdcrow. I hang in cornfields, wedgie-style, to keep the crows away. They would not be caught dead anywhere around me. For you see, despite my above average mathematical skills, I am not cool.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Actually, most would consider dragon-fruit to be that exotic, indeed. (Buford starts to imitate Baljeet) Known for its dazzling flowers, it is actually the fruit of several... (Sees Buford mocking him) What are you doing? St-Stop that. Uh-Ah-buh- (Baljeet starts drinking his smoothie, and Buford mocks him doing that as well) Stop that.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: ...and at the destabilization point, the vortex collapses in on itself, and it becomes an actual "hole" in space-time, sucking the nearest person or object into it and they are lost in the void.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: And it is so simple! I can use an ion coupling device to attract each atmospheric molecule to the second greatest gravity source, which in this case, is the moon, and after the initial impact...

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Yes! By my calculations, we have effectively strengthened the hydrogen bonds between water molecules, so that the surface tension is virtually unbreakable! In your face, physics camp! Booyah!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Phineas and Ferb, days ago, you helped me build a portal to Mars. Now, I beg you to help me win the Biggest Watermelon Contest at the festival. Help me, Phineas and Ferb. You're my only hope! (Looks around and then turns off his hologram)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (goes over to the dandelion and picks it) Hmm... (drawing on the fence) Two point seven-three-two times ten to the twenty-sixth power of particles. But I could not tell you the exact location of any of them because of the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I, too, have a question. If I miss the third shuttlecock with my rubber chicken, does Buford have to jump over the chokecherry bush before or after the girls finish peeling their tangerines?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Well, I got kicked out of summer school because my grades were too high. But then I heard about this place! Sure, they break you down and strip you of your identity, but school is school.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: From my observations, Candace's instability stems from her desperate need for attention, which she clearly is not getting from her mother. It is no wonder Candace is crying out for help.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: It looks like the next anomaly will appear any second now. I am working on the exact coordinates, but there is significant interference. It looks like there may be multiple rifts coming.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: So after hiding in the bathroom, I jumped out the window and came over here as quickly as possible. I do not even know how to act in front of a girl! I do not even know what girls like.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Oh, no! The portal is broken! Ooh, now I will not get a good grade at the science fair tomorrow, and, uh,... there's also the issue of your sister stranded on a distant, barren planet.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Ghosts, there is no such thing. Look! My EMF readings are three milligauss. Normal background radiation. And when we point it at the room, it is also... Well, that cannot be right.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Surface tension is the property which allows molecules of water on its surface to form a sort of stretchy skin, which allows it to retain its shape and durability at a small size.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Buford! You're completely disrespecting this classic song. You're ignoring the historical context! King Wenceslas was a great man. You have no idea what this song is about!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: No! There is always a way! Isabella teaches the emergency preparedness class for the Fireside Girls. She could build a generator in her sleep. Is that not right, Isabella? (who is not here)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Actually, you did, too. Since our planet's orbit of speed around the sun is 67,000 miles per hour and you are on its surface and speeding around the sun as well. (Buford spins the hat on Baljeet's head.) Quit it!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: We are so privileged to be here in this strange and beautiful place. To think that the greatest minds in history have been searching for Atlantis for thousands of years.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: This place must exist outside the flow of time. Candace, you were the only one of us outside the loop. Were the looping intervals decreasing in chronological amplitude?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: You are missing the point! I do not know that if I chose strawberry I would get hit by a bus! I am just saying that every decision we make has unforeseen repercussions!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I have an idea. (Wipe to him later on) Phineas and Ferb made me this 3D projector. I can project one of their projects right into the yard here. Your brother will think they just built it.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Your blueprints are 97% sound. But you accidentally placed a cosine where you needed a quadratic differential! (laughs) Not to worry. I fixed it. I will send an attachment.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: No can do, Phineas. I am taking an eastern Indian cooking class. We are going to make goat vindaloo. If we can ever find a goat. (goat brays offscreen) Oh! There is one now. Got to run! (runs away)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Yes, but now I've got to write her back in a passive way that makes her think it's really her idea. She is trying to manipulate the situation. (He takes another bite of his sandwich) It is how we love.

Name: Dr. Baljeet
Dialog: Well, since the Phineas and Ferb from the first dimension suggested we make the most of our summer, Buford and I have been experimenting with fun, and so far...

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I know this goes completely against all logic and therefore makes it totally out of character for me to say, but I think you may have been cursed with bad luck.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: "Haha" yourself. I am going to win this race! Oooohh! The impending victory! It is as sweet as... (Greg LeMond quickly passes him) Greg LeMond? I thought you were supposed to be motivating me.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Well, the slowly melting ice of the wheel creates a slick surface, eliminating friction. (Close-up on Baljeet.) Gravity converts into angular momentum, giving us perpetual mo—Hello?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Well, we have to build something to close the hole and stop the looping.  But it will require einsteinium, tungsten wire, and micro-crystal plasma resistors.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: No! I moved polka back so I could answer your question! It would take some major rearranging, but I think I can at least come to watch you make the bubble.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: She has absorbed too much water! She is nearly two tons! We cannot fire the device until she is close to her normal density! Otherwise she could explode!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Plot all you want, I have my eye on you! No one will be able to stop me from stripping away the Earth's atmosphere! Oh, the things I will be able to see!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Well, let us see. (transitions to Eiffel Tower) Oh, this is from the time Phineas and Ferb built a full-scale replica of the Eiffel Tower. I will hide the projector in the bushes.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: No, that is Venus. And that is Earth in prehistoric time. (Gasps, yells) Change it, change it, change it! Whoo, Hey, look, it is us in the future fixing the portal.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: You know, if I am good enough to impress the Katherine Marshall, maybe my acting talents are worth cultivating. Maybe I should take a class. Buford?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Well, folks, I do not know about Western cinema, but this Forced Perspective Western Town has been a hoot, which I am just now realizing is a thing.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (offscreen) HEEELP!!! (Runs onscreen) Help! Phineas and Ferb, and to a lesser extent, Buford! I am having an existential emergency! I find myself incapable of making decisions!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: For your safety, Mishti, I invite you to hold on to the rail. It appears to be very clean, which I know is important to you now that you are a girl.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (runs up) Phineas! Ferb! I saved Buford's life, and now because of the Bully Code, he is my personal servant! It is driving me crazy! You have got to help me!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Yes! Yes, it does! This way my work will not be interrupted by creatures who cannot possibly understand it! Like raccoons, or people, for instance.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (on radio) Not to add pressure to what is already a high-pressure system... (giggle) but we have six minutes and forty-one seconds 'til your mom dissipates completely!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I did it! I won a bike race! Thanks to Greg LeMond inspiring me. And then, you know, getting attacked by that tiger. By the way, I hope he is okay.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I said early. Anyway, under personal preferences, I could not decide whether to select 'Loop' or 'String' theory. I was paralyzed with indecision!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: When she looked at you, her pupils actually formed little hearts. Like, I do not know how that is physically possible. She changed her eyeballs!

Name: Baljeet-2
Dialog: I will try to keep it open for as long as possible, but the window is very unstable. Even the slightest disturbance could cause it to collapse.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: N-No! Of course not, sir. Hehe (walks off; comes back with a chicken-shaped out of peanuts) Here, sir. Try our deluxe peanut chicken. Our **motto** is: "So Peanutty, you will not even taste the chicken!"

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: That's because it is. Every minute of my entire day is planned out right here. Remember how you told me to seize the day? Consider it seized!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Thank you, Phineas. (Cut to the dining room. The gang is gathered around the table in their pajamas.) In researching for my very first slumber party, in which I am so excited to stay up past my regular bedtime of 9:30 p.m…

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Technically, we will not be drifting. More like violent ejection, plummeting through the atmosphere and crashing onto the planet's surface.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: The weight of your freakish muscles will only pull you down faster. And why does he just stare off into space like that? (screams) Phineas, help us!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (blinks) Huh. I had not noticed that. I acknowledge your accomplishment with limited praise as an emotionally-restrained mentor. Let us do this!!!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Seeing as there are 34 sheep in the circumference, if we calculate the sheep radius and multiplied by y divided by 3πr², you would get... (falls asleep on the ground, snoring.)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: But the part that perplexes me the most is that, for some reason, the sun algorithm that I created keeps coming up with the wrong result!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Well, I stand corrected. You seem to have a lot of information. But if you know so much about it, why do you not sing the original song?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Wrong. It is very primitive and aggressive. We do not want to meet it in here. (shows gazelles that look like Phineas and Ferb running away from the id.) Obviously, you see Phineas and Ferb as some sort of prey.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Perhaps we can give you a recharge, but, of course, this time with the correct powers. We have been working on rebuilding the machine.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Do not worry, Phineas. With all of her training, she will be fine. Just last week, she earned her Judo, Hapkido, and Jujitsu Patches.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: On a multi-valve engine with variable timing, how can I isolate an exhaust valve leak at the stem seal without removing the camshaft?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Uh my schedule is extremely tight. I doubt I even have a second to answer your question. Maybe if I move my polka recital back. Okay.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: By chance. I ran into the director, Katherine Marshall, and she thought I would fit a particular role. A character called "Exterra".

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (looking at a tablet) Inexplicably, your mother's vaporized bits have coalesced with the high humidity in the air to form a "cumulo-mom-bus" if you will.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I am not mechanically inclined like the two of you. To truly understand my predicament, I feel it will be best expressed in a song. (Claps hands twice)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (To Ferb) You know this is pretty tame compared to other roller coasters, but when you compare it to other dental themed rides, it is a rush!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Then, they put it all together to make you this salad. There are still grasshopper legs in it, but other than that, it is not bad.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I feel this may not be the best way to block a shot. Clearly I was - Clearly I was wrong about that. That was most effective. Aah!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: You know, Isabella, I sometimes wonder if it was mere coincidence that it was you and I chosen to portray the young, happy couple.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: While this Forced Perspective Town is charming, it has not changed my perspective. I still find the Western film genre tacky and— (screams as a giant tumbleweed runs him over)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: You will be most gratified. (Buford walks in) As long as you find insignificant bags of peanuts gratifying… (faceplams) Welcome to Wedgieville. Population: me.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Okay. (Baljeet makes some calculations.) Right... (pointing on a map) There! In fifteen seconds, that is the point of maximum disturbance! So it should be appearing right over...there! (A groundhog gets sucked into the rift.)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Ferb has discovered a way to temporarily alter road surface modules from a solid to a liquid state around the hull. Fascinating!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Aww! I got you in my tractor beam! (starts pushing buttons) Time to strip the atmosphere from our planet, and allow an unobstructed view of the cosmos!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Oh, that's it! I will become Hanuman Man, a flying blue monkey that can grow as massive as he desires to crush all in his way! (pause)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Do me a favor. Next time you want to make a fiendishly clever computer-controlled contraption, call one of your other friends.

Name: Dr. Baljeet
Dialog: All we have to do is get these magnetic deprogramming chips near the cyborgs' frontal lobes and they will no longer be evil.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Well, winning does take the sting out of the fact that there is obviously a horse out there somewhere with only three shoes.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Um, hello? Can we discuss the bigger problem? And by "bigger problem", I mean "THE BERSERK NECROSLUG THAT IS ON THE LOOSE"!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: We could remove you to a sterile environment and get a board certified surgeon to cleanly and safely preform a Jere-botomy.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: It is like our own miniature Canada! But, of course, without the beavers, moose, and disproportionate number of comedians.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: You know, saliva is 98% water and the other 2% is made up of very beneficial electrolytes. It is gross, but it is science.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: If by okay, you mean that my life is a meaningless, black cauldron of swirling failure... then yes, everything is groovy.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: And now, for my final trick, (cut to main stage) I will reattach my thumb! Feel the rhythm, feel the rhyme, come on thumb, it's healing time.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: You are amputating two perfectly good words and stitching them together. They are the Frankenstein monsters of grammar.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Last stop! I'm afraid there is no way to get to the East Coast by boat unless you go all the way around South America.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Finally, we have been able to harness the energy in raw vegetables to power the unicycle. But how will we make it fly?

Name: Baljeet's Brain
Dialog: I had discarded my limited physical form like a useless appendix! I will free everyone to create a mind-brain utopia!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Buford, these equations show that if we combine your brawn with my brains, we can conquer the final target together!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: There is a new Space Adventure movie filming in Danville. (takes out a poster) The Namrak Necroslug. And I have been invited to audition!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: But how? Mr. Random is already miles away. We have no idea where he is going and no way to get there except on foot!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Because of the 17 summer school classes I am taking, I qualified for the science fair. So I decided to design this.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: We're going to the circus! We're going to the circus! (Cut to the kitchen, where Phineas, Ferb, Isabella and Django is eating Pow cereal... aside from Buford) I am here and ready to go to the world-famous Cirque de Lune.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: ...I gotta get it, gotta g... gotta get it, gotta get it, gotta get it, gotta get it, gotta get it, gotta get it...

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (Sarcastically) And spoil my carefully calculated air of selfishness and unconcern? Not until the last second thank you very much! (Baljeet and Buford sail away leaving the rest of the group behind)

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Huh, if you convert the basal molecules into an adenosine triphosphate engine, it might be theoretically possible.

Name: Baljeetolas
Dialog: Greetings, adventurers! If by my bow, or my vast store of useless knowledge I may aid you... Hey, where is my bow?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Good, we will just wait here and eventually, the fuel will run out. (Isabella and Buford look at him) Ohh... And then she will plummet to...yeah...

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Hmm... maybe it is not too late. We should try to get them together. You know, before Isabella leaves for school.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: YES! I have BEAT you, Danville Mountain! In your cliff face! Ha ha! I cannot wait to tell Buf- oh. That is right.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (Seeing Buford fall) Oh no! Buford is in trouble! I must do something! (He goes to a man selling balloons) Please, my bully is in trouble, let go of all of your balloons.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I have been making mental notes of the paths and probabilities as I have gone along. It will be a piece of cake.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: So you are telling me that even though you are now a girl, you still like to have fun just like in the old days?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Ah! this is catastrophic! Should we not do something? Should no one inform the populous of the impending impact?

Name: Second Baljeet
Dialog: This is great! Now that I have made both choices, I will no longer miss any opp- (DBG bus returns, hits Second Baljeet) What do you know! I was right!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Huh. Usually, some unforeseen element would have removed our invention by now. Perhaps we should take it down.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Really? Because usually, people are either gone or fall asleep by the time I get to this part of the sentence.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (getting out a binder) …I present to you the ultimate sleepover checklist! Movies, a pillow fight, ice cream sundae bar, some mores (s'mores)…

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: You mean test the resiliency of our cartilaginous collusion with vigorous application of weight and velocity?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: (Holding a plastic dummy that looks just like him) Thank you. Thanking you much. So little Jeet, I hear you went to New Delhi. And did you try the chicken club?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I can see how that would be relevant if we were going to eat it. We are not going to have to eat it, are we?!

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: No, no please! I have given my solemn oath to protect the little monotreme until the Flynn family comes home.

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: I did not go through six years of ninja school just to be called Dr. Baljeet. It is Dr. Ninja Baljeet, okay?

Name: Baljeet
Dialog: Another week's allowance replacing wedgied underwear. If I had anything left, I would invest in the company.
